title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This act aims to protect the integrity of elections by setting up safeguards against AI-generated misinformation and deceptive content that could influence voters. It establishes detection methods, transparency requirements, and penalties to prevent AI from undermining democratic processes.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress should not give extra money or special rules to companies or banks that are on the brink of collapse because of the AI market; instead, it should help Americans who have been harmed by these events. The policy calls for directing support to those affected rather than providing bailouts to firms at risk.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to ensure that AI systems developed in the United States are reliable, safe, and transparent by setting standards and oversight. It likely includes provisions for funding research, establishing guidelines, and creating mechanisms for accountability and compliance.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to make the use of artificial intelligence within the Department of Veterans Affairs more open and understandable. It requires the VA to disclose the purpose, data sources, decision‑making processes, and potential biases of every AI system it uses, so veterans and stakeholders can see how AI affects their care and services.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act proposes rules to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in Veterans Affairs claims processing, ensuring that such systems are transparent, fair, and reliable. The bill aims to protect veterans by holding the VA and its contractors accountable for AI decisions that affect benefit outcomes.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard people from misleading or harmful AI content. It sets rules for creators and providers to be transparent, accurate, and accountable when using AI in consumer products.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to ensure that advanced artificial intelligence systems are developed and deployed safely, with rigorous security measures to prevent misuse and protect against cyber threats. It establishes guidelines, oversight, and compliance requirements for AI developers and users to maintain robust security standards and safeguard public interests.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act creates a dedicated group within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to evaluate and improve the security of artificial intelligence systems. This task force will work with industry, academia, and other government agencies to develop best‑practice guidelines, share information, and monitor emerging AI threats that could impact national infrastructure and public trust.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with AI systems to protect public safety and privacy. It mandates reporting, oversight, and compliance measures to ensure developers and operators follow secure development and deployment practices.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for coordinating the development, deployment, and oversight of AI‑controlled physical technologies, such as autonomous vehicles and robotic systems. It sets safety standards, creates oversight bodies, and requires collaboration among industry, government, and researchers to ensure responsible, interoperable, and secure use of these AI systems.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard democratic processes by limiting the use of AI to spread misinformation or manipulate voters during campaigns. It establishes rules and penalties to ensure AI-generated content used in elections is transparent, accountable, and cannot undermine public trust.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes a framework for overseeing AI systems that can modify and improve themselves. It requires developers to document changes, conduct safety checks, and report updates to regulators so that autonomous evolution of AI remains transparent, safe, and accountable.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act is a law that temporarily bans the creation and expansion of new AI data centers. It is designed to pause rapid growth while lawmakers assess the environmental, energy, and societal impacts of large AI computing facilities.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is proposed legislation designed to prevent autonomous AI systems from operating without human oversight in potentially harmful ways. It calls for strict safety protocols, accountability measures, and oversight to ensure AI development and use remain safe and aligned with human values.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a dedicated board tasked with overseeing cybersecurity risks associated with AI technologies. The act gives the board authority to investigate incidents, set safety guidelines, and coordinate with federal agencies to ensure responsible AI deployment.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act seeks to steer artificial‑intelligence development so that it benefits all citizens. It proposes policies that promote transparency, fairness, and public value in how AI is researched, built, and deployed.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is legislation aimed at overseeing the development and deployment of artificial intelligence within China. It seeks to establish guidelines and reporting requirements for AI systems to ensure compliance with national standards and security protocols.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at ensuring that only qualified medical professionals, not artificial intelligence systems, can provide certain types of medical care. It seeks to protect patients by restricting the use of AI in diagnosing and treating conditions that require human judgment and accountability.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy would set up a new office inside the President’s Executive Office to monitor and address threats from artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. This office would coordinate national responses and help develop guidelines to keep these rapidly evolving technologies safe and beneficial.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a new Select Committee dedicated to overseeing artificial intelligence. It outlines the committee’s mandate, membership, and responsibilities for guiding AI policy and regulation.
